## Direct Answer: SSC JE 2026 Answer Key & Paper-1 Expected Cut-Off

> [!IMPORTANT] **Core Update**: The Staff Selection Commission (**SSC**) has published the **SSC Junior Engineer (JE) Paper-1 Tentative Answer Key 2026** and candidate response sheets on **ssc.gov.in** for **1,699+ Engineering Vacancies** across CPWD, CWC, BRO, MES, and Farakka Barrage. Candidates can log in using their Registration Number and Password to calculate raw scores (**+1 mark** for correct answers, **-0.25 mark** negative marking). Based on shift-wise difficulty analysis and vacancy volume, the **expected Paper-1 normalized cut-off for Civil Engineering is 120–128 marks (UR)** and for **Electrical/Mechanical Engineering is 125–133 marks (UR)**.

Every year, lakhs of Diploma and B.E./B.Tech engineering aspirants compete in the SSC Junior Engineer examination for Group 'B' Non-Gazetted technical posts carrying **Pay Level-6 (₹35,400 – ₹1,12,400)** under the 7th Central Pay Commission. With the tentative answer key now live, calculating your exact raw score, auditing doubtful questions for official challenges, and benchmarking against past 3-year cut-offs is critical before starting full-throttle Paper-2 (CBT-2) technical preparation.

## How to Download SSC JE 2026 Response Sheet & Calculate Raw Score

1. **Visit the Official SSC Portal**: Open the unified Staff Selection Commission candidate login page at [ssc.gov.in Login](https://ssc.gov.in/login) or view our direct status tracker on the [SSC JE Answer Key 2026 Post](/job/answer-key-ssc-junior-engineer-je-answer-key).
2. **Enter OTR Credentials**: Input your **12-digit Registration Number**, Password, and the Captcha code, then click **Login**.
3. **Open Answer Key Challenge Module**: On your candidate dashboard, navigate to the **My Applications** or **Answer Key Challenge** tab under *Junior Engineer (Civil, Mechanical & Electrical) Examination 2026*.
4. **Download Response Sheet PDF**: Click the generated link to open your shift-specific Question Paper & Response Sheet. Save it immediately as a PDF, because SSC disables response sheet links once the objection window closes.
5. **Compute Your Raw Score**: Count your total correct attempts (`C`) and total incorrect attempts (`W`). Use the Paper-1 marking formula: **Raw Score = C − (0.25 × W)**. Leave unattempted questions at `0`.

> [!CAUTION] **Save Your Response Sheet Today**: Once the official objection window closes, the tentative response sheet link expires permanently on ssc.gov.in. Always download and back up a local PDF copy for rank prediction, normalization checks, and future objection verification.

## SSC JE 2026 Paper-1 Shift-Wise Difficulty & Good Attempts Analysis

Paper-1 comprises three sections: **General Intelligence & Reasoning (50 Marks)**, **General Awareness (50 Marks)**, and **General Engineering — Civil / Electrical / Mechanical (100 Marks)**. Across all shifts conducted in November 2026, candidate feedback and technical subject analysis indicate a **Moderate to Slightly Tough** technical section, particularly in code-based numericals and assertion-reason questions.

| Paper-1 Section | Total Questions | Max Marks | Weightage Share | Difficulty Level | Safe Good Attempts (90%+ Accuracy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 50 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:25%:Reasoning] | **Easy to Moderate** (Time-consuming seating/series) | **42 – 46 Questions** |
| **General Awareness (GS + Current Affairs)** | 50 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:25%:General Awareness] | **Moderate to Tough** (2025–26 Science & Schemes) | **24 – 30 Questions** |
| **Part-A / B / C: Technical Engineering** | 100 Questions | 100 Marks | [BAR:50%:Technical Branch] | **Moderate** (IS Codes + Conceptual Numericals) | **68 – 76 Questions** |
| **Total Paper-1 Composite** | **200 Questions** | **200 Marks** | **[BAR:100%:Total Composite]** | **Overall Moderate** | **134 – 152 Attempts (Net 122–135 Marks)** |

> [!TIP] **How Normalization Impacts Tough vs Easy Shifts**: Because SSC conducts Paper-1 across multiple shifts, raw scores are adjusted using SSC's official equi-percentile / mean-standard deviation normalization formula. Candidates who appeared in harder technical or GS shifts typically see a **+5 to +11 marks boost**, whereas easier shifts may see minimal change or a slight relative shift adjustment.

Unlike screening-only exams, SSC JE Final Merit is calculated on **Paper-1 (200 Marks) + Paper-2 (300 Marks) = 500 Total Marks**. If you are scoring near the borderline in Paper-1, you must aim for 230+/300 in Paper-2 to secure CPWD or MES allocation.

## How to Challenge Wrong Questions in SSC JE Answer Key (₹100 Objection Guide)

If you spot an incorrect official answer key option, an ambiguous Hindi/English translation discrepancy, or an out-of-syllabus technical formula error in your response sheet, follow this exact protocol:

1. **Verify Standard Proof First**: Never challenge a question on memory. Cross-check against standard reference textbooks (IS 456:2000 for RCC, IS 800 for Steel, B.L. Theraja / Ashfaq Husain for Electrical, R.K. Bansal / P.K. Nag for Mechanical, or NCERT for General Awareness).
2. **Access the Challenge Tab**: Log in at [ssc.gov.in](https://ssc.gov.in/login) and select **Raise Objection / Representation** next to your question ID.
3. **Upload Supporting Justification**: Select the exact Question ID, choose the nature of discrepancy (*Wrong Answer Key*, *Multiple Correct Options*, *Translation Error*), and upload a crisp PDF/image screenshot highlighting the standard textbook proof.
4. **Pay ₹100 Per Question**: Pay the non-refundable representation fee of **₹100 per challenged question** using UPI, Debit/Credit Card, or Net Banking.
5. **Download Payment Receipt**: Save the confirmation receipt. Remember: if even **one candidate** in your shift successfully challenges a flawed question, **SSC awards full/normalized benefit to all candidates in that shift** in the Final Answer Key.

## Next Step: Paper-2 (CBT-2) Strategy & Negative Marking Alert

Wait times between the Paper-1 Answer Key and Paper-2 exam are typically short (6 to 8 weeks). If your raw score sits anywhere within **5 marks below or above the expected cut-off**, begin **Paper-2 preparation immediately**!

| Paper-2 Exam Parameter | Official Rule for SSC JE CBT-2 |
|---|---|
| **Exam Mode** | Objective Computer-Based Test (100% Technical Engineering Only) |
| **Total Questions & Marks** | **100 Questions × 3 Marks = 300 Marks** |
| **Exam Duration** | **120 Minutes (2 Hours)** |
| **Negative Marking Penalty** | **-1 Mark** per wrong answer (1/3rd penalty — much stricter than Paper-1!) |
| **Virtual Calculator Allowed?** | **YES** — Scientific Virtual Calculator, Log Tables, and Steam Tables are provided on-screen! |

> [!TIP] **Master the 3-Mark Virtual Calculator Rule**: Since Paper-2 awards **+3 marks per question** and penalizes **-1 mark per mistake**, focus heavily on numerical precision using the on-screen virtual scientific calculator, IS Code provisions (especially IS 456, IS 10262, IRC standards for Civil; Power Systems & Machines for Electrical; Thermodynamics & Fluid Mechanics for Mechanical), and GATE/IES 1-mark & 2-mark previous year questions.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### Q1: When is the SSC JE 2026 Paper-1 Final Answer Key and Result declared?
**Ans**: After the 4-to-5 day tentative answer key objection window closes, SSC subject-matter experts review all ₹100 challenges. The **Paper-1 Result and Category-Wise Cut-Off** are typically published within **4 to 6 weeks** on `ssc.gov.in`, followed by the Final Answer Key and normalized scorecards.

### Q2: How is the SSC JE 2026 Paper-1 score calculated?
**Ans**: Paper-1 has 200 questions worth 1 mark each. Every correct answer earns **+1 mark**, and every wrong answer deducts **0.25 marks**. Formula: `Total Raw Score = (Correct Answers × 1) − (Wrong Answers × 0.25)`. Unattempted questions carry zero penalty.

### Q3: Are SSC JE Paper-1 marks added to the Final Merit List?
**Ans**: **Yes.** Both Paper-1 (**200 marks**) and Paper-2 (**300 marks**) are added together to compute your Final Merit Score out of **500 marks**. Scoring well above the Paper-1 cut-off gives you a crucial cushion for top ministries like **CPWD**.

### Q4: If one student challenges a wrong question in my shift, do I need to pay ₹100 too?
**Ans**: No, you do not have to pay separately if another candidate in the exact same shift has already challenged that specific Question ID with valid proof. When SSC accepts an objection and updates the Final Answer Key, **all candidates in that shift automatically receive the corrected marks** during final evaluation. However, challenging clear mistakes yourself guarantees the objection is submitted.

### Q5: What is the difference in Paper-1 cut-off between Civil and Electrical/Mechanical?
**Ans**: Historically, **Electrical and Mechanical** share a combined cut-off that runs **5 to 18 marks higher** than Civil Engineering because total vacancies in Civil (CPWD, BRO, CWC) are significantly larger than Electrical/Mechanical vacancies.

### Q6: Can Diploma holders get promoted to Executive Engineer or Gazetted Officer in CPWD after SSC JE?
**Ans**: Yes. After joining as Junior Engineer (Group 'B' Non-Gazetted, Level-6), candidates are promoted to **Assistant Engineer (AE — Group 'B' Gazetted, Level-7/8)** through departmental examinations and seniority, and subsequently to **Executive Engineer (EE — Group 'A' Gazetted)**.
